headline: Chips Lead, Crude Cools, and the Middle East Sets the Tone for Thursday's Open
body_html:
Wall Street heads into Thursday's open after a split Wednesday session, with 276 stocks rising and 254 falling across our 536-name universe. Chip shares did the heavy lifting, as semiconductors gained 1.56%, while homebuilders fell 1.48%, the weakest group we track.

The overnight backdrop is dominated by the Middle East. Crude eased on hopes for a diplomatic path even as worries about wider fighting linger, and an Iranian official reportedly called the latest mediation ideas unacceptable. European energy ministers are set to take up high fuel costs with winter approaching, and Israel's deadlocked election leaves the political picture unsettled. The Fed chair's firm line on inflation keeps rate worries in play.

At the open, watch whether the big single-stock moves hold. Genmab jumped 28.25% and Vertiv gained 16.48%, while F5 sank 20.43%, Landstar fell 17.76% and Enphase lost 16.03%. Traders will also see how GE Vernova trades after slipping despite stronger results and a higher outlook, and whether chip momentum tied to Micron's rally carries over.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors set the pace
briefs.body: Semiconductors were Wednesday's strongest group, up 1.56%. Within the space, Sandisk rose 7.66% and contract manufacturer Flex climbed 11.61%. Commentary on Micron's rally keeps memory and hardware names in focus as Thursday's session opens.

briefs.headline: Crude slips on diplomacy hopes
briefs.body: Oil prices fell as hopes for a peace track outweighed fears of a widening Middle East conflict. Refiner Phillips 66 reported a record quarterly profit on strong refining results, a reminder that margins, not just crude, are driving energy earnings.

briefs.headline: Fed's inflation stance stays in focus
briefs.body: The Fed chairman struck a tough tone on inflation, and bond investor Jeff Gundlach weighed in on the central bank's rate pause and talk of holding fewer policy-setting meetings. Rate-sensitive areas, homebuilders especially, may stay on edge.

briefs.headline: Sharp losses hit F5, Landstar and Enphase
briefs.body: The session's steepest declines came in single names: F5 lost 20.43%, Landstar System 17.76% and Enphase Energy 16.03%. CoStar fell 13.96%, Logitech 12.12% and Zurn Elkay 11.5%. Watch for any rebound or further selling at the open.

briefs.headline: Healthcare gains on Genmab surge
briefs.body: Healthcare rose 0.88% as a group, helped by Genmab's 28.25% leap, the largest gain in our universe. Ensign Group added 8.62%. The question for Thursday is whether the biotech move holds or sees profit-taking.

briefs.headline: Power and data-center names catch a bid
briefs.body: Vertiv Holdings climbed 16.48% and Forgent Power Solutions gained 8.45%, extending interest in the equipment behind AI infrastructure. GE Vernova slipped despite a stronger quarter and higher outlook, so the open should show whether buyers step in.
